conviction_note: No company-level number the market lacks; the filed items are proxies (index returns, BlackRock flows, FactSet's print) and a slightly lowered sell-side bar that together lean mildly positive on revenue against a known sustainability drag and a September/October AUM dip that weakens the exit run rate, so p_up 55 on an abs move of 7.0 (option event move 6.92, own median 5.69) gives +0.70, close to the +0.7 sum of the findings; the two measurements agree because nothing here is decisive.
bar: Q3 2026 adj EPS $5.02-5.03 and revenue ~$884-889M: Benzinga $5.02 / $883.8M (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/MSCI/earnings-forecasts), TickerLeague $5.03 / $886.2M from 8 analysts (https://tickerleague.com/companies/MSCI/estimates), Investing.com 2026-10-19 $5.02 / $887.8M (https://za.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/msci-earnings-in-focus-as-analysts-watch-margin-trajectory-93CH-4512075); Zacks lower at $4.99 / $880.3M (https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:66f90bf34094b:0-msci-set-to-report-q3-earnings-what-s-in-store-for-the-stock/). Two or more sources agree within $0.01, so the bar is sourced. Caution: the Q2 bar was disputed ($4.86 Benzinga vs $4.99 FactSet), and the stock traded the FactSet number and the revenue miss, so the revenue line ($870.7M consensus vs $867.0M reported in Q2) is the one this name trades on.
positioning_check: Short interest about 1.63% of float, about 1.3 days to cover (equibles, August 2026 settlement, https://equibles.com/stocks/MSCI); an earlier mid-2026 snapshot read 2.46% / 3.2 days. Not crowded, so there is no squeeze mechanism either way. Baseline skew is +0.8 vol points (25d put minus call), close to balanced; the sweep row's +5 is stale. Put/call OI is 2.93 on a thin 1,668 contracts. Event-implied move is 6.92% (Unusual Whales showed +/-7.66% on 2026-10-06). Spot 560.83 is 12.9% below the 52-week high after the -10.1% reaction to Q2; run-up is -1.26% over 5 days and +0.33% over 20 days. The sell side cut targets into the print (Morgan Stanley 700 to 662 on 2026-10-13, JPMorgan 700 to 685 on 2026-10-14) while staying Buy-rated: 16 of 18 analysts are Buy, average target ~$673.

findings.finding: Q3 index-linked AUM inputs, from public index returns: ACWI ETF total return July -0.3%, August +2.7%, September -1.2% (quarter about +1.2%); EAFE +1.7%, +1.8%, -3.3% (about +0.1%). MSCI's own Q2 release puts June-30 ETF AUM linked to MSCI equity indexes at $2,818B, 4.1% above the Q2 average of $2,706B. Inflows were 'nearly $40bn' in Q2, and management called early-Q3 inflows 'exceptional'. Q3 average AUM therefore sits roughly 5-7% above the Q2 average, which implies asset-based fee revenue up about $12-16M QoQ. Consensus revenue of $884-889M is +2.0-2.5% QoQ (+$17-22M) on Q2's $867.0M; with subscription growth of about 2% QoQ plus First Street, that looks covered, with a small upside of about 0.5%. Against that, the September decline leaves the quarter-end ABF run rate only about flat-to-+3% QoQ, and ACWI is -0.6% in October to date.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue is the line this stock trades on. It beat revenue in only 3 of the last 8 quarters (tickerleague). In Q2 2026 revenue missed by $3.7M (with an expense-guide raise) and the stock fell -10.14% despite record AUM. Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 prints rose +5.69% and +5.37%.
findings.why_not_priced: MSCI-linked AUM is tracked by every covering analyst, so the direction is largely in consensus: revenue estimates rose 0.4% over two months. What may not be in it is the exact Q3 average versus the September exit. If the market had priced a clear ABF beat, revenue estimates would sit above $890M and the stock would not be 13% off its high with targets being cut.
findings.independence: The Q2 base comes from MSCI's own release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001408198/000140819826000044/exhibit991earningsrelease-.htm). EAFE returns are from https://chartrow.com/msci-eafe/monthly-returns. This shares the market-data series with no other finding.

findings.finding: BlackRock's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-14), after MSCI last spoke, reports $135B of iShares net inflows with 'broad-based strength across iShares ETFs'. BlackRock is MSCI's largest ETF licensee. The flows were led by bond ETFs ($61B) and precision ETFs ($41B), and equity-index flows are not broken out, so the read-across to MSCI equity-index-linked ETF flows is positive but indirect.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Record ABF and ETF flows in Q2 (+25% ABF run rate) did not stop a -10% reaction to a revenue miss and expense raise, so flow strength alone has not bought the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for five days and widely read, so mostly priced. The residual is that the analysts who cut targets on 10-13 and 10-14 published around this release. If the read-across were fully priced, MSCI would have rallied with BLK, and the 5-day run-up is -1.26% instead.
findings.independence: Different company and document from finding 1, but the same AUM transmission, so the two are partly correlated; secondary summary at https://pulse2.com/blackrock-q3-2026-results. This is a proxy, not an MSCI number.

findings.finding: FactSet's fiscal Q4 (quarter to 2026-08-31, reported 2026-09-30) showed organic ASV +7.0%, above the top of its own guidance, with ASV growth across institutional buy-side, wealth and dealmakers and retention above 95%. That points to stable buy-side data budgets through August, which bears on MSCI Analytics (Q2 organic run-rate growth 6.6%, retention 94.3%, net new sales $11.2M, management calling the H2 pipeline 'pretty strong'). But FactSet guided FY27 organic ASV to 5.0-6.5%, below the pace just achieved and below consensus, so the forward read is mixed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Analytics sales softness ('lumpiness') was part of the Q2 sell-off narrative. No clean record of the stock moving on Analytics alone.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer print three weeks old is visible, but the read-across to MSCI's Analytics net new sales is not a line any consensus tracks. If it were priced, Analytics retention and sales expectations would have moved up, yet EPS estimates fell 0.3% over two months.
findings.independence: MSCI's own Q2 call said the H2 Analytics pipeline is 'pretty strong' (https://www.webull.com/news/15266275730072576). FactSet's FY27 guide below consensus cuts the other way (https://finviz.com/news/397092/factset-shares-fall-35-as-fiscal-2027-guidance-comes-in-below-expectations). This is a proxy.

findings.finding: MSCI guided on the Q2 call that Sustainability & Climate recurring net new sales would be 'roughly zero to slightly negative' over Q3 and Q4, with Americas cancellations a 'significant headwind' and a 'protracted cyclical downturn'. In Q2 the segment had $1.9M of net new sales against $7.4M of cancellations, 92.3% retention and 3.2% organic run-rate growth. First Street (closed 2026-08-03) adds about $10M of run rate to the segment, as already guided. The segment is roughly a tenth of subscription run rate while Index grows 11.1%, so net of the rest the drag is small, and it sits inside what the company told the market.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Softer sustainability sales commentary was one of the drivers cited for the -10.14% Q2 reaction (https://www.tikr.com/blog/msci-nyse-stock-tumbles-after-second-quarter-earnings-and-revenue-miss-wall-street-targets).
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: it is guided and widely repeated in previews. The residual risk is a quarter at the 'slightly negative' end, or a retention print below Q2's 92.3%. If the market expected worse, the skew would be bid for downside, and at +0.8 it is not.
findings.independence: First Street closing confirmed by https://ir.msci.com/node/22881. Shares the Q2 call transcript with finding 6.

findings.finding: The sell side trimmed into the print: Morgan Stanley cut its target 700 to 662 (2026-10-13), JPMorgan 700 to 685 (2026-10-14), both keeping Buy ratings. Consensus EPS fell 0.3% over two months while revenue estimates rose 0.4%, and Zacks shows the EPS estimate down 0.39% over 30 days. MSCI has beaten EPS consensus in each of the last four quarters (average +1.85% per Zacks). So the earnings bar was lowered slightly while the revenue bar crept up.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 'beat' on one EPS source was a miss on FactSet's, and the stock fell 10%. EPS-beat history has not protected the stock when revenue or expenses disappoint.
findings.why_not_priced: Target cuts are public, so this is mostly priced. The point is that expectations are being managed down on EPS: a lowered bar with an unchanged business raises the odds of a print above it. If the cuts reflected a known miss, EPS estimates would have fallen more than 0.3%.
findings.independence: Zacks preview (https://www.tradingview.com/news/zacks:66f90bf34094b:0-msci-set-to-report-q3-earnings-what-s-in-store-for-the-stock/) shows the same downward EPS drift; same aggregator family, so partly shared.

findings.finding: The fee rate on asset-based fees keeps drifting lower. Management said in Q2 that growth was concentrated in lower-fee developed ex-US and all-country products and that the bps fee 'is going to be dynamic' (period-end 2.28 bps). The January 2026 BlackRock licence amendment changed fees from 2026-01-01, with further changes from 2027-01-01. Q3 flows in EAFE/ACWI-type products continue that mix, which trims ABF dollars per unit of AUM.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Fee compression was flagged by analysts on the Q2 call, which the stock sold 10%; it was not isolated as the driver.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the amendment is nine months old and the Q2 bps is public. The residual is how far the Q3 mix pulls the bps below 2.28. If the market had a larger compression in its numbers, revenue estimates would not have risen 0.4%.
findings.independence: Q2 call comments on mix and fee rate (https://vectorshift.ai/research/companies/msci/earnings/2026-q2) share the Q2 call with finding 4.

findings.finding: The expense guide was raised in Q2 (operating expense $1,535-1,575M from $1,490-1,530M; adjusted EBITDA expense $1,340-1,370M) for First Street, AUM-linked incentive compensation, D&A and revolver interest. The guidance assumed a Q3 close, and First Street did close on 2026-08-03, inside that assumption. AUM-linked accruals should be no higher than guided after September's index decline. A second raise is not indicated by any document found.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 expense-guide raise was the most-cited cause of the -10.14% reaction, so this name punishes expense raises hard.
findings.why_not_priced: It is inside guidance and so priced as guided. It is filed because it is the line with the largest proven reaction, and either a further raise or a trim to the guide moves the stock. Nothing found says which.

findings.finding: The CFO (Andrew Wiechmann) sold 450 shares at $570 on 2026-10-12 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2025-09-03, leaving 21,644. Separately, an 8-K of 2026-08-07 made him interim principal accounting officer after the Global Controller/CAO departure first disclosed on 2026-03-31. The CEO bought shares in February and May 2026, but no open-market purchase appears after the July drop: the Form 4 list since July shows only filings on 09-01 (three), 09-04 and 10-14.
findings.why_not_priced: Trivial size and pre-planned. The absence of a CEO buy after a 10% drop is mildly informative only against his record of buying dips (Feb and May 2026).

outside_window.finding: EU ESG Ratings Regulation: MSCI notified ESMA on 2026-07-02 that it intends to apply for authorisation as an ESG rating provider. The application deadline is 2026-11-02 and ESMA's final RTS report came out 2026-10-15. Any authorisation outcome and its compliance cost land after the exit window.

baseline_tension: Nothing found cuts against the balanced skew (+0.8) or the flat 20-day run-up; the mild positive lean sits inside a market that has priced roughly symmetric outcomes, and the stock's large two-way reaction history (median 5.69%, last move -10.14%) means the sign will be set by revenue versus $884-889M and by any change to the expense guide, neither of which a document found here settles.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (inside the guide): the sustainability finding is inside what management guided, so it moved from -0.3 to -0.2.
Lesson 5 (proxy sized small): the BlackRock flow read-across is bond-led and not broken out by equity index, so it moved from +0.4 to +0.3.
Lessons 3/5 (caveat reaches the number): FactSet's FY27 guide below consensus offsets its ASV beat, so that finding moved from +0.4 to +0.3.
Lesson 7 (positioning): the lowered EPS bar is public, so it moved from +0.3 to +0.2.
Lessons 1/2: the AUM revenue finding stays +0.3 because the reaction history shows revenue is the line traded; the expense-guide finding stays at 0 (lands on guidance, no document either way).
Lesson 6 (bar): confirmed by three agreeing sources ($5.02-5.03), so no cap was needed.
